title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the table of contents of a ~90-page manuscript, 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}'. It sets out a programme for describing the boundary ('the structure at infinity') of the moduli stacks of curves of genus g with ν marked points, combinatorially and groupoid-theoretically.

The progression:
(1) 'Standard curves'. The next page defines these as quasi-projective curves over an algebraically closed field whose only singularities are ordinary double points. Each has a canonical smooth completion, with points at infinity I and nodes A.
(2)-(3) The dual graph of such a curve ('M-graph'), then stable curves and their 'MD-graphs' (Mumford–Deligne graphs). These are the stable dual graphs indexing the boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification M̂_{g,ν}.
(4) Recall of Deligne–Mumford theory.
(5)-(6) Specialisation of MD-graphs (edge contraction, i.e. closure relations between strata) and 'generalisation morphisms' of graphs. This is a category of stable graphs, essentially the modern category of stable graphs with contractions used for the boundary complex.
(7) Explicit determination of the graphs for M̂_{g,ν} of modular dimension 3g−3+ν ≤ 2.
(8) Specialisation structure of strata in ambient modular dimension ≤ 4. This concerns how the low-dimensional pieces fit together, in the spirit of the 'two-level principle' of the Esquisse.
(9)-(10) The 'MDT-structure': a groupoid structure on the open Teichmüller modular multiplicities. It is done first transcendentally, then analytically, with generalisation morphisms acting. This amounts to Teichmüller groupoids with base points at the boundary strata, and maps between the fundamental groupoids of strata and their neighbourhoods.
(11) A digression on 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a normal-crossings divisor, giving the structure at infinity of fundamental groupoids. This is plausibly a real-oriented-blow-up / tubular-neighbourhood construction that produces boundary (tangential-type) base points and the local tori at the deepest strata.
(12) The combinatorial types attached to a normal-crossings stratification, and their dévissage into 'elementary types' ('locks'/'blocks'?).
(13) A digression on general stratifications. This links to the later 'tame topology' and stratified-spaces themes of the Esquisse.

The problem served is the Teichmüller tower / Galois action programme. The aim is to reconstruct the system of fundamental groupoids of all M_{g,ν} from low-dimensional pieces, glued along boundary strata indexed by MD-graphs.
errors: No mathematical claims are made on this page (table of contents only), so there is nothing to check for correctness.

missed.claim: The manuscript plans a general theory of the 'unfolding' of a normal-crossings divisor as the tool for describing fundamental groupoids at infinity. This is the role later played by Kato–Nakayama spaces and real oriented blow-ups in the Ihara–Nakamura / Hain treatments of the Teichmüller groupoid. If the notes (pp. 52–74) are early (c. 1981), this is an unpublished anticipation.
missed.quote: Digression : déploiement d'un diviseur à croisements normaux. Structure à l'infini des groupoïdes fondamentaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These pages could give a Grothendieck-style, functorial construction of boundary base points for stacks with normal-crossings boundary, of possible interest for log-geometric anabelian work.

missed.claim: The plan includes an explicit analysis of specialisation of strata up to ambient modular dimension 4. This is presumably his own attempt to justify the two-level principle, which the Esquisse states without proof.
missed.quote: Structure des spécialisations des strates en dim. modulaire ambiante ≤ 4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing it with Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps could show whether Grothendieck had a proof strategy different from theirs.

missed.claim: A dévissage of combinatorial types of normal-crossings stratifications into 'elementary types' (annotated 'locks' or 'blocks'), followed by a digression on general stratifications.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This may anticipate the cone-complex / tropical combinatorics of boundary strata; the content on pp. 74–90 would need checking.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a table of contents. It confirms the existence of a detailed unpublished treatment of the material sketched in the Esquisse, including a 'déploiement' digression that may anticipate later log/real-blow-up methods. But no content is visible on this page.
